subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic delayed/batch agent-turn contract across provider runtime, Plugin SDK, gateway protocol, and background execution surfaces, or intentionally defer provider Batch API support?
rationale: The request crosses public API, provider auth eligibility, session/transcript state, delivery timing, fallback behavior, config/protocol fields, and provider-specific implementations, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design generic delayed turns
options.body: Add a provider-neutral delayed-turn lifecycle first, then implement OpenAI and Anthropic Batch API support through that seam for cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat.

options.title: Limit to cron/provider shortcut
options.body: Implement a narrower cron flag faster, accepting higher risk of inconsistent provider behavior and later migration work.

options.title: Defer Batch API support
options.body: Keep real-time execution as the supported agent-turn behavior and document why provider Batch APIs are out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Design generic delayed turns
recommendation.body: Add a provider-neutral delayed-turn lifecycle first, then implement OpenAI and Anthropic Batch API support through that seam for cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the provider runtime, Plugin SDK, isolated cron execution, and session-tool boundaries that need the first design decision.
